reviews.reason: Gathering transfers existing exposed stock; it does not assess or separate bark. Root preparation consumes no new tree material and cannot supply its own implements. A small bark-assessment and separation capability is therefore missing. The observed tree currently exposes branch stock, not a demonstrated bark reserve: neither its name nor inspection alone may create bark. Development can provide assessment and a material-conserving branch-peeling precursor without assuming successful extraction or supplying tools.
reviews.experienceReview: Inspection, requesting, learning and obtaining a label award nothing. Paid assessment or separation that genuinely establishes previously unknown, personally observed material behavior may emit information-confirmed through the existing probe-equivalent qualification logic, with evidence and qualified=true only for new verified information. Reuse grounded-understanding, not a second bark-specific source: the observing actor receives amount 0.8, cap 1, duration 8 rounds, refresh repetition and cooldown 12; qualified continued experiments contribute the existing maintained gain 0.035 with decay 0.0015. Repeating an established fact does not qualify. Ordinary repetitive peeling provides no automatic pleasure or maintained satisfaction: it is effortful material acquisition, and useful output alone does not demonstrate enjoyment. Health, hunger, fatigue and protected mental accounts remain independent.
reviews.visualReview: Show assessment uncertainty and explicit material/tool failures, not a successful bark icon before extraction. Bind process visuals to the declared start, progress, completion and stop events: display the real branch, diminishing outer layer, separated bark quantity, residual core, tool reservation and remaining paid work. Replay must reconstruct conserved input/output amounts and cancellations from those events. Use actual ground-stack positions and existing shared collision/interaction rules; a work marker is non-solid and supplies no shelter, comfort or invented room effects. Leave the observed standing tree visually unchanged when only an already gathered branch is peeled.
reviews.specification: Implement bark-extraction@1 with public arguments {action: assess|peel|inspect|cancel, targetId, toolId?, quantity?: positive number, processId?}. Shared references use persistent actor, object, stack and process IDs, world coordinates, dt, existing interaction distance and shared collision geometry. Individual learning is required. Reuse gather's stock-transfer and root-preparation's reservation/progress code separately from this new function; neither code reuse grants those abilities or changes their contracts. Dependencies: actual branch/material composition, ownership, tool hardness/contact geometry, inventory capacity, source stock, persistent process and event systems. Assess costs one round and 0.2 energy, requires visible target within its actual interaction boundary, and reports retained physical facts, uncertainty, required tool and estimated recoverable mass. It does not extract material. Inspect full retained tree/material state before migration: preserve all known composition and source history. An unknown standing trunk receives no invented bark reserve and remains ineligible for trunk stripping. Minimal executable precursor: gather an actual exposed branch through the existing gather interface, then peel that owned branch. Introduce a conservative layered model for otherwise composition-unspecified branch material: at most 10% of its existing mass is separable outer bark, with the remainder woody core; partition existing mass, fuel and provenance rather than adding biomass, and record this explicit model assumption. Known contradictory composition overrides this default. Never apply the model to previously separated material or replenish peeled fractions. A standard 1.1-mass branch can thus yield at most 0.11 mass, or 0.366666 bark units at the existing 0.3 mass/unit; do not round upward or claim this meets root-preparation's one-unit requirement. Peeling requires an owned actual stone or flint implement with hardness at least 8 and a usable contact edge confirmed by assessment; absent prerequisites yield an actionable failure, not supplied items. For each original branch unit, require two work-rounds at one energy each, linearly scaled for fractional quantities. Reserve selected branch material and the reusable tool atomically in actor-owned process escrow; retain ownership and prevent simultaneous use. Each paid work increment separates the proportional bark mass and updates remaining layer mass, woody-core mass, actual work remaining and provenance. Preserve total material mass and partition chemical fuel without duplication; do not let stripped core re-enter the unmodified branch recipe or regenerate bark. Outputs retain source IDs, processing history and age; no nutrition or toxicity is erased by relabeling. Completion requires all declared paid work and transfers only actual separated bark and residual core to available inventory capacity, otherwise leaving owned outputs at the work location. Progress requires a living actor, sufficient energy, access to escrow and continued interaction range. Loss of access or energy pauses; cancellation or death terminates work, releases the tool, and leaves completed bark plus partially peeled material with their actual remaining work and ownership at the process location. No escrow is cloned, deleted or reset by death or respawn. Do not modify standing-tree health or geometry during this precursor; future trunk removal requires separately represented finite tissue and wound effects. Declare bark-assessed, bark-peeling-started, bark-peeling-progress, bark-peeling-completed and bark-peeling-stopped events, with process/source/output IDs, paid energy, transferred mass, progress and failure reason; retain existing information-confirmed validation. request.name: Obtain usable bark from an observed tree
request.function: Assess and, when physically feasible, remove a small usable piece of bark from an actual nearby tree for use as a reusable root-preparation implement.
request.conditions: I am near tree object:region-1-canopy-18 at (55.4,14.2). Observation showed two accessible branches but no bark resource. I own three roots, no stone or bark, and have mastered root-preparation. Bark availability and safe extraction are unknown.
request.inputs: An actual suitable tree; any necessary tools or material requirements must be established rather than assumed.
request.costs: Unknown; specify actual effort, duration, tool requirements and tree damage or other risks before use.
request.effects: If feasible, transfer only physically obtained usable bark into inventory, accounting for source changes. Do not grant bark merely for inspection or naming, and report infeasibility if current conditions do not support extraction.

input.contextPolicy: Object IDs refer to deduplicated actual applicant observations. Whole records are selected with omission counts. Missing detail is unknown, not proof of absence. Full retained state is available during the development handoff; implementation must validate actual prerequisites and ownership.
input.implementation: New interfaces, state, geometry, persistent processes, rendering components and personal memory/task adapters can be delivered through a versioned current-conversation handoff. Source validation and history must remain intact. Declared implementation does not supply stock, objects or mastery.
